name: codegraph-qa labelling protocol 1
consensus: truth is an answer given by at least 2 of opus, sol and astra; astra is asked only where opus and sol both answered and disagree; cannot-tell never counts; a site with no consensus is reported with its rate, never imputed
blinding: one call site per question, candidates shuffled per item by sha256 and unattributed (no subject or oracle named), fixed answers W (other in repo), X (outside the repo), Y (local binding), Z (cannot tell); the repository copy hides .git, .codegraph, node_modules, expectations and agent instruction files

prompt.hashed: the prompt rendered for the fixed item {id: 'protocol', site: site.ext:1 NAME, candidates: [c.ext:1]} with no repository, so the hash changes exactly when the template does; identical at every commit from 660d8ff (qualification) to the samples

opus.runtime: Claude Code CLI -p, tools Read/Grep/Glob only, empty HOME (no instructions, hooks or MCP servers)

sol.runtime: Codex CLI exec, read-only sandbox; MCP servers, apps, web search, image generation and AGENTS.md off

astra.role: tie-breaker on opus/sol disagreements (same family as sol: tables report which side it takes)

kimi-k3.runtime: harness runtime, read-only repo tools, LiteLLM gateway; serving deployment recorded per turn

probe: every run first asks the labeller for its tool list and refuses it if any tool reaches beyond read-only repository access (labels/run.mjs)

qualification.items: known-answer items from fixtures/oracle-candidates (labels/qualify-items.mjs): a fixture's right edge is the truth, its wrong targets and same-named definitions are the distractors

labelled.note: UTC last-write time of each answer file in the run's working directory; answers carry no timestamp of their own
